notes: The tutorial says 'any MKR family board'; arduino-mkr-wifi-1010 was chosen as a representative board. Its pins 1, 2, 3, 4 and GND are assumed to plug into the shield's matching header sockets.

The MKR Relay Shield is not in the catalogue, so it is a new part type. Relay 1 is wired internally to pin 1 and relay 2 to pin 2. The relay coil/contact switching (COM to NO/NC) and the other pass-through header pins are not modelled.

The circuit image for the optional LED circuit (IMG05) was not provided. I assumed this layout: pin 3 -> 220 ohm resistor -> LED 1 -> GND, and pin 4 -> 220 ohm resistor -> LED 2 -> GND. The resistor value (220) and the breadboard hole positions are assumptions.

Fix for the V4 error: the three ground wires (wire3 from the MKR GND, wire4 and wire5 from the LED cathodes) now use three different holes on the same ground rail (tn.1, tn.2, tn.3) instead of all sharing tn.1. A rail is one strip, so the electrical connectivity is unchanged.
The 24V power supply and 24V lamp example on the relay screw terminals (IMG07) is described only as an illustration, and no image was provided, so it is not part of the graph.
